candidates.title: Imaging hot-electron Thomson cooling beyond the Boltzmann–Onsager framework
candidates.authors: Xinrong Zuo, Guokang Zhang, Weikang Lu, Anish Das, Guijian Pang, Ziyi Xu, Ludi Qin, Chengfeng Ding, Hongtao Xu, Siyu Duan, Ziteng Zhang, Pingping Chen, Wu Li, Zhenghua An
candidates.abstract: Classical Thomson cooling, constrained by lattice-dominated heat dissipation and the weak entropy variation of charge carriers under thermal equilibrium, remains inefficient within the Boltzmann–Onsager framework. Driving electrons far from equilibrium broadens their energy spectrum and smears the Fermi edge, and this amplifies the temperature dependence of the electronic entropy. However, the hot-electron thermoelectric response beyond the classical thermal equilibrium limit has remained unexplored due to the lack of direct access to hot-electron dynamics. Here we image spatial distributions of electron and lattice temperatures together with the corresponding thermoelectric signals in HgTe and HgCdTe nanoconstrictions using coupled scanning-probe techniques. In HgTe, weak electron–phonon coupling allows hot electrons to remain far from thermal equilibrium with the lattice, and this generates large electron temperature gradients and a pronounced Thomson compensation effect. In HgCdTe the response shifts towards lattice-mediated heat redistribution due to the suppressed non-equilibrium state. These observations reveal a pronounced departure from the conventional near-equilibrium Boltzmann–Onsager expectations in high-field thermoelectricity, identify the Thomson effect as a key channel of non-equilibrium energy dissipation and establish a platform for exploring non-equilibrium thermoelectric phenomena in nanoscale conductors. Classical Thomson cooling is inefficient. Now non-equilibrium energy dissipation with a breakdown of the Boltzmann–Onsager limit is demonstrated by imaging hot electrons in HgTe and HgCdTe quantum wells.

candidates.title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
candidates.authors: Connor Heimig, Thomas Weber, Cristina Cruciano, Armando Genco, Thomas Possmayer, Luca Sortino, Gianluca Valentini, Cristian Manzoni, Maxim V. Gorkunov, Giulio Cerullo, Alexander A. Antonov, Andreas Tittl
candidates.abstract: Abstract Anisotropic van der Waals materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, enabling tailored directional light–matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS 2 ) stands out among them for its strong in-plane anisotropy and thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons. These excitons can hybridize with light to form exciton–polaritons, rendering ReS 2 a compelling material for nanophotonic integration. Metasurfaces are arrays of subwavelength resonators and can support ultrasharp quasi-bound states in the continuum resonances. Topological transformations of their band structure can give rise to flatbands, which host dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Here we show that structuring ReS 2 into a resonant metasurface reshapes its photonic band topology, splitting the integer topological charge of the quasi-bound states in the continuum into two half-integer polarization singularities and driving the formation of directional far-field flatbands. Tuned into resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS 2 , these flatband states hybridize into distinct directionally polarized exciton–polaritons. This points towards a scalable route to polarization-resolved quantum emitters, flatband-enhanced nonlinear optics and low-threshold polariton devices.

candidates.title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
candidates.authors: Meng Gao, Deping Guo, Ang Li, Renhong Wang, Zhitong Jin, Chun Huang, Yixiang Lu, Yuhao Pan, Jiuxiang Dai, Panqi Huang, Kangjie Liu, Cong Wang, Lihong Bao, Lin Zhou, Jingsi Qiao, Wei Ji, Stephen J. Pennycook, Hong-Jun Gao, Wu Zhou
candidates.abstract: Two-dimensional metal oxides offer a versatile platform for exploring quantum phenomena and enable functionalities beyond those of their bulk counterparts. Despite advances in synthesizing ultrathin and free-standing oxides, controlled fabrication at the single-atomic-layer limit has remained a formidable challenge. Here we report the controlled fabrication of diverse free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides (MO), including CrO, ErO and BiO, down to the single-atomic-layer limit via electron-beam-induced dehalogenation of layered metal oxyhalides (MOX). Using monolayer CrO as a representative system, which features a single-atomic-layer square lattice, we obtain free-standing single-crystalline domains exceeding 104 nm2 and demonstrate controllable patterning at the micrometre scale. Density functional theory confirms both the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of free-standing monolayer CrO, predicting a Néel antiferromagnetic order below 230 K. Combined experimental and theoretical analysis reveals that ionization-driven halogen selective removal and lattice relaxation underpin the CrOCl-to-CrO transformation, a conversion mechanism potentially extendable to other metal oxyhalides. This approach further enables the fabrication of MOX–MO lateral heterostructures as well as aligned and twisted metal oxide bilayers, which exhibit pronounced excitonic responses with an unusually large exciton binding energy. Our work opens opportunities for two-dimensional metal oxide monolayers, heterostructures and moiré superlattices, and for exploring emergent excitonic phenomena in low-dimensional oxides. The electron-beam-assisted subtraction method enables the controllable fabrication of free-standing metal oxide monolayers, along with lateral heterostructures and twisted bilayers, expanding the material space of 2D quantum systems.

candidates.title: Glacial CO2 drawdown by plankton metabolic balance
candidates.authors: B. B. Cael, Malte F. Jansen, C. Mark Moore, Matthew B. Osman, Jamie D. Wilson
candidates.abstract: Which mechanisms caused the Holocene-versus-Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) difference? This longstanding question is crucial for characterizing glacial-interglacial cycles and using LGM climate information in climate predictions. We argue that the metabolic temperature dependence of epipelagic plankton is an important mechanism. Autotrophic plankton metabolisms are less sensitive to temperature than heterotrophic ones. Colder waters can thereby export and thus sequester more carbon in the deep ocean. We develop a theoretical model from Metabolic Theory of Ecology principles, then validate its predictions with empirical data compilations. We then use temperature reconstructions to estimate the plankton metabolism-driven LGM CO2 anomaly. Holding all other conditions at their pre-industrial state, such as net primary production and buffering capacity, we find that this mechanism represents a 6.2 ± 0.9ppm per degree global mean sea surface temperature change feedback, and can potentially explain 20 ± 5ppm, or ~ 1/4 of the total ~ 90ppm LGM CO2 anomaly. We diagnose a similar 18ppm using model data from an intermediate complexity Earth System Model that considers glacial-interglacial differences in nutrient limitation and primary production. Our findings are consistent with several temperature-driven mechanisms acting concertedly to modulate glacial-interglacial CO2 variations. In colder waters, plankton respiration slows down more than photosynthesis does, meaning more photosynthetically fixed carbon can sink to the deep ocean. It is estimated that this effect explains about a quarter of the CO2 drop during the last ice age.

candidates.title: Stabilization of insulin receptor mRNA by Star-PAP in metabolic homeostasis
candidates.authors: Na Chen, Yuxiao Zhao, Yanru Chen, Muye Tong, Weiqiong Gu, Jie Hong, Yansong Liu, Nan Yin, Peng Lu, Mengshan Ni, Zhiyin Zhang, Danjie Li, Yufei Chen, Shaoqian Zhao, Aibo Gao, Jie Zheng, Min Cao, Bin Cui, Yufang Bi, Weiqing Wang, Hong Cheng, Jieli Lu, Guang Ning, Ruixin Liu, Jiqiu Wang
candidates.abstract: Conserved polyadenylation b3y poly(A) polymerases (PAPs) is essential for mRNA stability, yet its metabolic functions remain unclear. Here we identify a rare variant p.D469N (Asp469Asn) in Star-PAP present in lean individuals but absent in obese cases. Adipose-specific Star-PAP knockout mice develop progressive adipose tissue loss, hepatic steatosis, and severe insulin resistance, phenocopying human lipodystrophy. Mechanistically, Star-PAP directly binds the insulin receptor (InsR) mRNA 3’–UTR to stabilize its transcript. Both deletion of Star-PAP and p.D469N variant decrease InsR mRNA maturation. Star-PAP deficiency impairs insulin receptor signaling and adipocyte lipid storage, while restoring InsR in adipocytes partially ameliorates the lipodystrophic phenotypes. Notably, Star-PAP deficiency disrupts acetyl-CoA homeostasis secondary to insulin signaling defects, accompanied by reduced histone acetylation at fatty acid synthesis genes. Pyruvate supplementation effectively restores acetyl-CoA levels and histone acetylation, thereby rescuing the gene expression and lipogenesis. Together, our results identify Star-PAP-mediated RNA polyadenylation as a mechanism governing adipose mass, positioning Star-PAP as a key regulator of insulin receptor signaling and lipodystrophy. Poly(A) polymerases (PAPs) are key regulators of mRNA stability. Star-PAP stabilizes insulin receptor mRNA to maintain adipose health and its loss causes lipodystrophy and insulin resistance, while pyruvate rescues the defects, highlighting RNA polyadenylation as a key to adipose homeostasis.

candidates.title: Proximity labeling of the Listeria monocytogenes surface reveals pathogen control of a host deubiquitinase
candidates.authors: Patrick J. Woida, Maisie W. Smith, Rebecca L. Lamason
candidates.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes navigates a crowded intracellular environment by recruiting host factors to its surface in order to hijack the host actin cytoskeleton for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Although these types of Listeria-host interactions are critical for infection, systematic characterization of this interface has been limited. Here, we implement the biotin ligase split-TurboID to profile host proteins recruited to the surface of L. monocytogenes during intracellular infection. We show that the host deubiquitinase CYLD is enriched at the pathogen surface. While CYLD promotes infection by suppressing innate immunity in macrophages, how L. monocytogenes recruits and appropriates CYLD function in other cell types has remained unclear. We demonstrate that L. monocytogenes uses the secreted effector Internalin C (InlC) to redirect CYLD to M1-linked linear ubiquitin at the bacterial poles. Despite its localization, CYLD does not deubiquitinate bacteria or regulate autophagic clearance in epithelial cells. Instead, CYLD and InlC protect L. monocytogenes from IFN-γ- and RNF213-dependent restriction of cell-to-cell spread. Overall, our work profiling the bacterial surface-host interactome has identified a mechanism by which InlC spatially reprograms CYLD activity to promote cell-to-cell spread in epithelial cells. These findings highlight how L. monocytogenes exploits a host deubiquitinase to perform cell-type-specific functions during infection. The pathogen Listeria monocytogenes recruits host proteins to its surface within infected cells for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Here, Woida et al. adapt the split-TurboID technique to identify such proteins and show how a secreted effector co-opts a host deubiquitinase to counteract host restriction of bacterial spread.

candidates.title: A training-free, domain-extensible LLM-based approach for automated extraction of standardized preparation procedures
candidates.authors: Daniel P. Costa, Matteo Manica, Teodoro Laino, M. Filipa Ribeiro, Pedro S. F. Mendes
candidates.abstract: Millions of synthesis procedures have been published, but their meta-analysis, important for identifying successful synthesis patterns, is difficult due to varied reporting structures. Using this information requires converting unstructured text into a precise sequence of actions, which requires understanding domain jargon, a challenge usually addressed by fine-tuning models on labeled data. We present a simple, training-free workflow for laboratory action extraction that works across fields, encoding domain knowledge through explicit action sets and using powerful, readily available Large Language Models, or LLMs. Applied to zeolite synthesis, a widely used class of porous materials, our approach outperforms existing open-source tools and delivers context-aware results with open, locally runnable LLMs. It also matches state-of-the-art, field-specific models in their own domains, highlighting the generalization capabilities of current LLMs. The methodology showcased, along with the open algorithms made available, allow chemists to evaluate action sets, screen LLMs, and digitize laboratory procedures accurately with minimal effort. A domain-agnostic, training-free workflow leverages open-source large language models with explicit action sets and post-processing rules to extract laboratory procedures from unstructured text, demonstrated through zeolite synthesis.

candidates.title: Viral tRNA-like structure hijacks host ribosomes for poly(A)-independent translation
candidates.authors: Guoliang Lu, Liming Wan, Yuchen Chen, Ye Li, Yajie Yan, Yan Liu, Zihan Wu, Ningyuan Zhang, Jinzhong Lin
candidates.abstract: Positive-sense RNA viruses often use 3′ tRNA-like structures (TLSs) instead of poly(A) tails to capture the host translation machinery. While TLSs resemble canonical tRNAs and engage host factors, their ability to directly recruit ribosomes has remained unresolved. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy snapshots of the histidine-accepting TLS (TLSHis) from tobacco mosaic virus bound to the tobacco 60S subunit, the 80S ribosome, and the 80S-tRNAiMet initiation complex. Across these states, TLSHis is consistently anchored to the L1 stalk of 60S, even under cycloheximide treatment, yet remains dynamic on the 40S subunit. Structural analysis shows that TLSHis transitions from the E-site to an adjacent Z-site to accommodate initiator tRNA. Functional assays show that TLSHis preferentially associates with ribosomal subunits over polysomes and can substitute for a poly(A) tail to promote robust cap-dependent translation. These results provide structural and mechanistic evidence that the viral tRNA mimic exploits the tRNA-exit channel to stabilize initiation-competent ribosomes and drive poly(A)-independent translation. Some plant RNA viruses use 3′ tRNA-like structures to promote translation without poly(A) tails. Here, the authors reveal how the tobacco mosaic virus tRNA-like structure directly engages host ribosomes to facilitate translation initiation.

candidates.abstract: Abstract When eukaryotic cells divide, a mitotic spindle, composed of microtubule filaments interacting with molecular motors, self-assembles and is responsible for aligning and segregating chromosomes to the opposite daughter cells. Recent structural studies revealed that spindles are composed of short microtubules that do not span the full pole-to-chromosome distance. It remains unclear how these short, disconnected microtubules collectively assemble a bipolar spindle. Using cryo-electron tomography to map microtubule polarity in human spindles, we find that microtubules organize with consistent 8 nm wall-to-wall spacing. Spacing scales inversely with local microtubule density, consistent with organization by density-driven steric interactions, analogous to liquid crystal ordering. We find that the Eg5 motor establishes local antiparallel overlap independently of spindle bipolarity, while a balance of Eg5 and dynein regulates microtubule density to maintain spindle architecture. Together, these findings reveal the mesoscale principles by which cells build complex, self-healing cellular architectures from nanoscale building blocks.

candidates.title: Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions
candidates.authors: Seung Hwan Lee, Shaowen Chen, Andrew T. Pierce, Patrick R. Forrester, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Amir Yacoby
candidates.abstract: Two-dimensional material platforms host a remarkable array of exotic correlated phases. Probing magnetic order in these systems is essential for understanding their underlying physics, yet dilute spin densities render conventional magnetic probes ineffective. Spin waves, or magnons, in quantum Hall ferromagnets (QHFM) have proven effective for probing the magnetic order in various symmetry-broken quantum Hall (QH) phases in graphene systems, but previous works have been limited to homojunction configurations within a single material. Here, we demonstrate magnon transmission across a monolayer-bilayer graphene quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunction—the first magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions, using one material as a magnon source to probe magnetic order in a distinct material. Generating magnons in monolayer graphene (MLG) at νMLG = 1, we detect their transmission through bilayer graphene (BLG) via nonlocal voltage measurements, revealing spin order in BLG symmetry-broken quantum Hall states. The transmission exhibits hallmark magnon signatures: a sharp onset at the Zeeman energy and systematic variation with Landau level filling, including suppression at νBLG = 4 and 8 where spin polarization vanishes. Our findings establish heterojunction magnon transmission as a powerful, modular probe of magnetic order, opening new avenues for investigating exotic quantum states across the rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional materials. Magnons in quantum Hall ferromagnets can be used as a very sensitive probe of magnetic order. Thus far, this technique has only been applied to single material systems. Here, Lee et al extend this to a heterostructure, using magnons generated in a monolayer of graphene to detect spin order in bilayer graphene.

Experiments confirm this trade-off across prompt designs, model hyperparameters, and evaluation paradigms. A structured collaboration model, in which the LRM broadens diagnostic coverage and the clinician verifies reliability, increases diagnostic accuracy by 20% and reduces false positives by 44% in a 15-physician validation study. These results, obtained under controlled retrospective conditions, suggest that pairing LRM reasoning with physician oversight may support safer and more accurate diagnostic decision-making, warranting prospective validation before clinical deployment. This study finds that reasoning-enabled AI models improve diagnostic accuracy but produce more false positives and less consistent outputs but physician oversight helps retain benefits while reducing safety risks.

This study shows that high vaginal albumin in vulvovaginal candidiasis is not merely a correlate of inflammation, but can drive dysfunctional hyperinflammation by promoting fungal induced inflammasome activation, while compromising fungal clearance.

candidates.title: Global arable land redistribution toward the tropics and drylands under human settlement expansion
candidates.authors: Lun Gao, Xiaoman Lu, Weston Anderson, Corey Lesk, Elise Mazur, Fred Stolle, Peter Potapov, Francesco N. Tubiello, Steffen Fritz, Jiafu Mao, Liangzhi You, Deepak Ray
candidates.abstract: Arable land extent has undergone widespread changes across many regions worldwide through processes such as urban encroachment, forest conversion to agriculture, and dryland farming expansion. Yet an integrated understanding of global arable land dynamics remains limited. Using our self-developed arable land product integrated with global human settlement layers, Köppen–Geiger climate classifications, and historical land-use reconstructions, we show that the disproportionate climatic co-location of arable land and human settlements fundamentally structures global arable land dynamics. Across much of the climatically favorable Northern Hemisphere, earlier co-development of settlements and agriculture has increasingly shifted toward competition, with settlement expansion displacing cultivation from temperate regions and contributing to its expansion into adjacent arid zones. In contrast, low-latitude tropical regions continue to expand both systems at the expense of natural landscapes, partly driven by agricultural investment from Northern Hemisphere. Globally, these contrasting trajectories reveal a broader redistribution of agricultural pressure from climatically favorable regions toward less-exploited tropical and arid environments, linking settlement expansion and agricultural displacement to diverse environmental consequences including deforestation, biodiversity loss, groundwater depletion, and vegetation greening. These findings highlight the need to consider both local settlement–agriculture competition and broader agricultural redistribution when planning future food production and settlement growth. Arable land is changing through urban encroachment, forest conversion and dryland expansion, but these shifts are often viewed separately. The study demonstrates a unifying framework for global arable land redistribution and its environmental consequences.

candidates.authors: Xingxing Zhong, Mian Wei, Jing-Kai Wang, Yuqing Zhang, Xiaoyan Jiang, Jianhua Yu, Xiang Zhao
candidates.abstract: Abstract The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned- acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D 2h ligands with lower-symmetry C 2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned- acs ), with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ) 1/3 . The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C 2 H 2 /CO 2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg −1 vs 0.98 mol kg −1 ).

candidates.abstract: Abstract Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

Therefore, we propose layer-wise prediction for interpretation method (LPI), which involves mapping the representation from each layer to a probability distribution, explaining the hidden-layer prediction process. To ensure interpretation fidelity to DNN mechanisms, we employ a reconstruction strategy to map probability distributions back to hidden layer features while reducing their influence on model prediction. Meanwhile, we define a rank-index metric to quantify the consistency of probability distribution evolution. Furthermore, we show how each hidden layer probability distribution evolves consistently during DNN forward propagation. Experiments on various models show that LPI achieves superior performance in consistency, stability, fidelity and certainty, outperforming AdditionalLayer, SDN, MetaGF, and DFS. Notably, LPI not only enhances deep learning interpretability but also provides valuable insights into reliable and credible model security assessment. Here, the authors introduce a hidden-layer interpretation method that maps intermediate DNN representations to probability distributions and reconstructs features to ensure faithful explanation.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide can increase charge density in scaled capacitors, but its high coercive field limits the low-voltage, high endurance switching required for dynamic random-access memory and embedded ferroelectric memories. Here we show that plasma-engineered (111)-textured TiN electrodes with N-rich, oxidation-resistant surfaces suppress interfacial oxidation and enable robust switching in 5 nm Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 capacitors. The devices exhibit saturated hysteresis at 0.6 V, with 2 P r = 31.5 μC cm −2 and E c = 0.62 MV cm −1 , and no hard electrical breakdown through 10 12 bipolar cycles. Their nucleation-limited switching kinetics extrapolate to sub-nanosecond polarisation reversal at DRAM-relevant capacitor areas. At 1.1 V, circuit simulations of a common plate 1T–1 C cell yield short- and long-term stand-by sensing margins of 482 and 201 mV under a 20 fF bit line load. Electrode texture and interface engineering therefore enable low-voltage, high speed switching without compromising endurance, mitigating the practical Kay–Dunn scaling penalty and the speed–endurance dilemma.

candidates.authors: Liping Liu, Tianlai Xia, Rachel K. O’Reilly, Shichang Chen, Zaizai Tong
candidates.abstract: Polymer lamellar crystals commonly consisting of folded chains are frequently formed since they are kinetically favorable. Hence, the metastability of polymer crystals can be regulated by crystallization pathways, and the thinner lamellar crystals display a tendency to transform into thicker crystals via lamellar thickening process. Herein, we report that photoresponsive two-dimensional (2D) platelets with low metastability undergo controllable fragmentation upon light irradiation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the metastability within a single platelet particle is heterogeneous across different domains. Light irradiation triggers lamellar thickening preferentially within less stable domains decorated with photoresponsive molecules, leading to site-specific fragmentation. To illustrate the utility of light-stimulated fragmentation, wavelength selective fragmentation of 2D segmented platelets with spatially defined photoresponsive molecules is achieved upon light irradiation, yielding 2D hollow platelet structure. This important feature holds significant promise for advanced applications such as spatially resolved therapeutic delivery systems, thereby broadening the functional scope of 2D nanomaterials. Two-dimensional platelets are typically formed from polymer lamellar crystals, with metastability regulated by crystallization pathways. Here, the authors report photoresponsive platelets with low metastability, which undergo controllable fragmentation on light irradiation.

candidates.title: Increasing prevalence and expanding diversity of tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella in China
candidates.authors: Weiwei Li, Tingting Yang, Qingpo Cui, Baisheng Li, Li Zhan, Xiaotong Jiang, Shaofei Yan, Lu Liu, Xiaoxia Qin, Zhihong Liu, Luyu Ying, Bo Yu, Xin Qiao, Xiang Huo, Meng Zhang, Weiwei Chen, Xin Lu, Yunchang Guo, Mengjiao Fu, Zhangqi Shen
candidates.abstract: The plasmid-mediated tigecycline resistance gene tet(X4) threatens the efficacy of tigecycline. While prevalent in Escherichia coli across diverse ecological niches, its evolutionary trajectory in Salmonella remains underappreciated. Here, we conducted nationwide genomic surveillance of 42403 clinical nontyphoidal Salmonella isolates collected from diarrheal patients in China between 2014 and 2025, of which 102 were tet(X4)-positive. Although the overall prevalence remained low, detection showed a statistically significant upward trend over 2019-2025. Importantly, the newly accrued 2025 data were broadly consistent with short-term forecasts generated by the beta regression model, providing partial support for short-term trend consistency. Genomic analyses showed that tet(X4) remained concentrated in ST34 but was also detected in additional sequence types, including ST469, ST8971, ST11 and one isolate with an unassigned ST, across multiple provinces, indicating broader geographic representation and genetic diversification. Plasmid analyses likewise revealed broader replicon diversity, with the dominant IncHI1A/IncHI1B/IncFIA background accompanied by less frequent IncHI2/IncHI2A, IncI1(Alpha) and IncFIA/IncFIB/IncFIC. Phylogenetic analyses further revealed shared clustering of the dominant plasmid background across host species and bacterial genera, consistent with cross-host and cross-genus circulation. Here, they determine that tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella remains rare in China but is being detected more often and in a wider range of bacterial sequence types and plasmids, supporting continued surveillance.

candidates.title: Secondary organic aerosol formation from sequential oxidation of toluene and cresols
candidates.authors: Aliisa Ojala, Aurélien Le Bayon, Avinash Kumar, Netta Vinkvist, Anni Savolainen, Anna Kervinen, Karine Sartelet, Matti Rissanen, Siddharth Iyer
candidates.abstract: Cresols are important urban emissions that can form multiple oxygen containing condensable vapors when they react with OH radicals in the atmosphere. These molecules contribute to secondary organic aerosols that have strong implications on climate and human health. In this work, we present flow reactor oxidation experiments demonstrating the rapid (sub-second) formation of condensable vapors with up to 10 oxygen atoms from the three cresol isomers (ortho-, para- and meta-cresol) under atmospheric conditions. Our quantum chemical calculations reveal that initial OH additions to the hydroxyl containing carbon atom lead to geminal diol intermediates that are critical to the rapid formation of condensable vapors from cresols and their key oxidation product, 3-methylcatechol. Incorporating these autoxidation mechanisms into model simulations shows that they contribute significantly to secondary organic aerosol composition. These results could explain the strong multi-generational contributions to aerosol from toluene and cresol, enabling a more accurate assessment of their climate and health impacts. Cresols and their oxidation products contribute to secondary organic aerosol, but their role in atmospheric oxidation remains poorly quantified. The authors report rapid formation of highly oxygenated organic molecules from cresols, identifying autoxidation mechanisms that could explain substantial multi-generational contributions to toluene and cresol secondary organic aerosol.

candidates.title: Exaiptasia diaphana core microbiome members are lost under climate change conditions despite host thermal tolerance
candidates.authors: Kaden Muffett, Stephen Williams, Sophia MacVittie, Mara JW Schwiesow, Susan Arechiga Mendoza, Salma Arechiga Mendoza, Hailey Hatch-West, E. Maggie Sogin
candidates.abstract: Abstract Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. We exposed two lines of the sea anemone, Exaiptasia diaphana , to acute and chronic thermal stress to quantify the impacts on cnidarian physiology and microbiome composition. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs.

candidates.title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
candidates.authors: Lina Antenucci, Chandan Thapa, Salla Virtanen, Timo A. Lehti, Annsy Arredondo, Ilona Pitkänen, Benita Westerlund-Wikström, Helena Tossavainen, Perttu Permi
candidates.abstract: Abstract Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus . Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus . Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus .

candidates.title: Retarding efficiency loss upon scaling in perovskite photovoltaics as fill factor becomes the bottleneck
candidates.authors: Buyi Yan, Ruihao Gong, Yanchun Huang, Nannan Gu, Runfeng Li, Dongxue Liu, Kangrong Yan, Xuehui Xu, Yang Michael Yang, Jizhong Yao, Dongchen Lan
candidates.abstract: Abstract Perovskite solar cells approach crystalline-silicon efficiencies at small areas, yet substantial performance losses during scale-up hinder their translation into practical modules. Here we quantify the contributions of device-performance parameters to efficiency loss during scale-up across diverse perovskite technologies, identifying fill factor ( $${FF}$$ F F ) as a major contributor and target for mitigating this loss. Further analysis resolves the FF deficit into voltage-, diode-non-ideality- and transport-associated contributions. Cryo-controlled processing provides an experimental route to preserve $${FF}$$ F F by regulating intermediate-phase evolution during crystallization. The resulting $${FF}$$ F F -preservation advantage arises predominantly from reduced diode non-ideality, with the other contributions being smaller. This advantage increases across device scales. A mini-module (19.48 cm 2 aperture) achieves a record certified steady-state efficiency of 23.9% with an $${FF}$$ F F of 83.3%, the highest reported for perovskite modules. The same $${FF}$$ F F limitation governs operational performance decay, linking efficiency retention during scale-up with long-term stability. Together, these results establish $${FF}$$ F F preservation and the factors governing it as central to mitigating performance loss during scale-up and operation.
